title: RREQ independent hex parse uses dataclass defaults for hop/flags/sig
description:
CORRECTNESS review of independent wire-hex parse tests in python/tests/loadng/test_messages.py (after worker6-4a8y).

test_rreq_from_bytes_parses_unsigned_hex_wire (lines 217-233) is the advertised independent 36-byte RREQ oracle, but the chosen wire is flags=0x00, hop_limit=4, signature=b"". Those are exactly RREQ dataclass defaults (flags=0, hop_limit=INITIAL_HOP_LIMIT=4, signature=field(default=b"")). seq_num is required and addresses are non-default, so only those three fields are actually proven parsed from the hex.

A from_bytes that unpacked only seq/originator/destination and left hop_limit/flags/signature at defaults would still pass this test. test_rreq_known_vector parse (hop=4, flags=0, empty sig) has the same gap. test_from_icmpv6_parses_hand_built_bodies RREQ uses the same body and does not even assert flags or signature.

Contrast: RREP unsigned hex uses flags=0x01 and hop_count=3 (defaults are 0, 0). RERR unsigned hex uses flags=0x80 and error_code=2 (defaults are 0, 0). Signed RREQ uses hop=8/flags=0x02, and hop-bounds uses 0 and 15, so the suite as a whole is not blind — this specific independent-hex RREQ vector is.

Related coincidence in the same from_icmpv6 test: RREP body flags=0x01 equals LoadngCode.RREP (1), so asserting flags==1 does not distinguish body flags from the ICMPv6 code. RERR body flags=0x00 (default) and flags is not asserted, while the ICMP code is 2.

Do not re-file 4a8y (to_bytes as oracle; signed/truncated/sig-tail coverage is present) or e3r3 (hop>15 parse).

Fix: give the RREQ unsigned hex (and from_icmpv6 RREQ body) non-default flags and hop_limit, e.g. flags=0x02 hop_limit=8 seq=0x012c, and assert them. For from_icmpv6, pick flags that are not equal to the ICMPv6 code (RREP flags != 1, RERR flags != 0 and != 2) and assert flags and empty signature on every success path.
close_reason: unsigned RREQ hex and from_icmpv6 RREQ use flags=0x02 hop=8 seq=0x012c; from_icmpv6 flags != ICMPv6 codes; flags and empty sig asserted. pytest tests/loadng/test_messages.py: 62 passed.
